sentences.text: There is delay of 137 days in filing the appeal.

For the reasons stated in the application duly supported with an affidavit of Assistant Manager of the Company namely Deepti Joseph, W/o Sudhir Joy Joseph, I.A. No.10382/2023 is allowed and the delay in filing the appeal is hereby condoned.

This miscellaneous appeal is filed by the Insurance Company being aggrieved of award dated 22/11/2022 passed by learned 5th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Chhindwara in Claim Case No.84/2018 on three grounds; namely, delay in lodging of FIR, not taking into consideration the aspect of contributory negligence and awarding compensation to the claimant- Dilawar treating him to have suffered 50% disability.

entities.text: 5th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Chhindwara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Shri Prakhar Naveriya, learned counsel for respondent No.1/claimant, appears on caveat and supports the award.
He submits that there is no illegality in the impugned award calling for interference.
3. On the merits of the case, it is evident from para-15 of the award that learned Claims Tribunal has dealt with the aspect of delay in lodging of FIR.
FIR was lodged by Tansingh alias Sandeep who is brother of the injured- Dilawar.

It is mentioned in the FIR, itself, that injured was grievously hurt,
therefore, after admitting him at District Hospital, Chhindwara, on being referred, he was taken to Nagpur for treatment and after return from Nagpur, report was lodged.
Thus, there is justification for delay of 27 days in lodging the FIR.
There is no material to controvert this aspect.

In fact, the principle of law is that delay should not be so exorbitant to prevent the Investigating Officer to investigate the case properly or to jeopardize the evidence in such a manner that the dependents are not in a position to verify the facts of the case.

When delay in FIR which is of 27 days is tested on the aforesaid two principles of law, then delay cannot be said to be exorbitant to be fatal to the case of the claimant, therefore, first ground deserves to be rejected and is hereby rejected.
4. As far as aspect of contributory negligence is concerned, there is no evidence on record.

On the contrary in para-21 of the award, learned Claims Tribunal has dealt with the aspect of a notice to the vehicle owner under Section 133 of Cr.P.C. Reply to the notice, motor vehicle owner admitted accident taking place on the fateful day in the hands of his relative Dharmendra who had borrowed the car.

Thus, there is an admission of accident and there is no pleading of contributory negligence on behalf of the owner of the offending vehicle, learned Claims Tribunal has rightly discarded the plea of the insurance company in regard to contributory negligence.
5. Now coming to the third aspect of 50% disability as has been considered by learned Claims Tribunal.
In para-31, learned Claims Tribunal has discussed evidence of Dr. Kaliram Verma (AW-4).
He has deposed that disability certificate of injured Dilawar was prepared by the Medical Board in which he was one of the members.
His signatures are present on the disability certificate.
He admitted that Board had found 80% disability caused to claimant- Dilawar.

In para-32 referring to The Oriental Insurance Comapny Ltd. vs Dilawar on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3662522/

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar, (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This finding too is not controverted by producing any cogent evidence or other evidence, therefore, all the three aspects having been dealt with by learned Claims Tribunal in a proper manner do not call for any interference.
6. Accordingly, this miscellaneous appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
(VIVEK AGARWAL) JUDGE ts
